evidence.claim: Paper overstates similarity of Milky Way and dSph dark-matter densities from D-factors, improperly inferring density equality from similar D-factors.
evidence.excerpt: The Figure 1 caption says that because the Milky Way and dSph D-factors have similar order of magnitude, “the density of DM in our galaxy does not differ much from the dSphs galaxies.” A D-factor is a line-of-sight integral of density with geometric and angular dependence; it is not simply a local density. Similar D-factors do not by themselves imply similar dark-matter densities.
